thread:
maria: Heads-up — running a POC with AcmeCorp and they hit a 401 on our /v1/generate endpoint after rotating keys. They say the key is the one we gave them in the POC creds bundle. Can eng help?

sasha: tagging jeff/kevin. Any logs from the proxy or auth service?

jeff: I can take a look. Maria can you paste the curl and the response body?

maria: here's what their SE sent: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-poc-acme-123" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"hello"}'
```

Response: ```json
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not found for org: acme-corp"}
```

maria: they also attached a screenshot showing the project selector in the console still lists the POC project id poc-acme-42

kevin: quick thought — did we rotate the key for that POC and issue a new binding to a different org/project? If the token was issued against a different org, the key will 401 when checked against the org-scoped route.

sasha: also saw similar last week where proxy cached an old binding. There's a cache TTL for key->org mapping (60s) but in edge cases a stale mapping can survive longer after rotation.

jeff: I'm pulling logs for key sk-poc-acme-123 now (searching auth-service and edge-proxy).

idp-bot: [audit] key-check request id=req_0a9f, key=sk-poc-acme-123, result=NOT_FOUND, checked_at=2026-03-20T15:04:12Z

jeff: auth-service shows the key was soft-deleted yesterday at 2026-03-19T22:18:03Z and replaced with sk-poc-acme-321. That would produce invalid_api_key on validation.

maria: customer insists they didn't rotate anything. SE says they just clicked “reissue” in the UI — could that cause a replace rather than a new parallel key?

kevin: the console 'reissue' flow deletes old key then creates new one (to avoid orphaned keys). If their client retried during the short window, they'd get 401. But if they still have the old token in their app it will keep failing.

sasha: any chance they're hitting a regional endpoint mismatch? We recently added region routing that can reject keys if bound only to a particular region.

jeff: checked region — key was global. This is just deletion/replacement.

maria: ok — action items I can run with the SE: 1) have customer paste the exact key they're using; 2) try the new key sk-poc-acme-321 in curl; 3) if they need old key back, we can temporarily re-enable it while they rotate.

kevin: from security/compliance we prefer not to re-enable deleted keys. Offer them a migration window and support to rotate. If they urgently need access, we can issue a short-lived emergency key scoped to the POC project (30m TTL) and audit the issuance.

maria: pricing question landed too — they asked if Dedicated reserved capacity affects POC throughput guarantees. Quick answer for SE?

sasha: POC on hosted API is best-effort throughput; Dedicated provides reserved slots and SLA. For short-term POC we'll offer a temporary Dedicated eval (1 week) at discounted rate — need AE approval.

maria: noted, I'll follow up in the sales thread. Back to auth — jeff, any preference for a support-playbook message I can send to the SE?

jeff: short playbook: 1) confirm key string, 2) try new key, 3) if 401 persists collect proxy trace id (x-rw-trace) and forward to eng, 4) escalate and we can issue emergency key with logged justification. 5) advise to update client to new key and rotate off old.

maria: perfect. I'll ping SE with that and include the emergency-key option. Thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin: also add a note for customer about token scopes — some POC keys are created with limited scopes (generate only). If they attempt embedding or admin calls with a generate-only key they'll see permission errors (403). Not the case here but good to mention.

maria: good call. I'll include scope checklist and quick curl tests for generate vs embeddings.

sasha: last note — I'll add a short test to the POC onboarding script to confirm the key works across regions and endpoints so SEs catch this earlier.

maria: thanks team, closing this swarm. I'll update the deal thread with outcomes and next steps.
